thread.title: Michigan Bought Intel and IBM Stock, and Sold Apple and Alibaba - Barron's

title: Michigan Bought Intel and IBM Stock, and Sold Apple and Alibaba - Barron's
text:
Michigan Bought Intel and IBM Stock, and Sold Apple By Feb. 4, 2019 7:00 a.m. ET Order Reprints Photograph by David Becker/Getty Images Text size
A Michigan agency that oversees over $11.1 billion in U.S.-traded securities recently made some big fourth-quarter stock trades.
The Treasury Department of Michigan’s Bureau of Investments is the asset-management arm of the Department, and serves as the fiduciary of the State of Michigan Retirement Systems and Michigan boards and agencies. The agency bought Intel stock (ticker: INTC) and International Business Machines stock (IBM), while selling Alibaba Group Holding stock (BABA), AT&T stock (T), and Apple stock (AAPL).
The Bureau disclosed the trades in a form filed to the Securities and Exchange Commission on Friday. Apart from Intel, all these stocks ended 2018 in the red, but all five have gained so far in 2019.
Michigan’s Treasury Department declined to comment on the transactions.
The Bureau bought 231,900 additional Intel shares in the fourth quarter, ending 2018 with 2.28 million shares of the chip giant. Intel stock eked out a 1.7% gain for the year, which was marked with a replacement of the top executive . Interim CEO Bob Swan was formally named to the post last week . Through Friday’s close, Intel stock is up 3.8% so far in 2019.
IBM stock limped to end 2018 with a 26% loss. Barron’s said the stock was a bargain in September , but IBM’s mixed results , and its agreement to buy Red Hat (RHT), pressured the stock late in the year. The state agency may have sensed opportunity when it bought 154,800 IBM shares in the fourth quarter, to end the year with 635,287 shares. The purchase looks particularly savvy, as IBM stock has surged nearly 18% year to date.
The Bureau more than halved its Alibaba stake by selling 139,132 American depositary receipts of the Chinese Internet giant in the quarter, ending the year with 100,061 ADRs. Alibaba lost about a fifth of its market value in 2018, as a trade dispute between China and the U.S. worsened and Alibaba founder and Executive Chairman Jack Ma retired from day-to-day operations . Alibaba ADRs have rallied nearly 23% so far in 2019 as trade talks have been lifting hopes for a deal.
Insiders were buying AT&T stock in the summer of 2018, but the purchases were apparently early. Shares of the media and telecom giant slid to a 52-week intraday low of $26.80 the day after Christmas, and AT&T stock ended the year nearly 27% in the red. The Bureau sold 415,164 AT&T shares the fourth quarter to cut its investment to 2.15 million shares. Fourth-quarter subscriber numbers reported in January came in light, but AT&T stock is still up 5.1% so far this year.
Apple stock slipped nearly 7% in 2018, as the company’s suppliers warned of weakness and President Donald Trump mused about slapping tariffs on the company’s iPhones . The Michigan agency sold 378,400 Apple shares in the fourth quarter, and ended 2018 with 2.02 million shares. Early in the new year, Apple warned of what many knew: iPhone demand was down , particularly in China. Yet Apple stock has gained 5.6% since the end of 2018.
(Editor’s note: This article has been updated to note that the Michigan‘s Treasury Department declined to comment.)
